transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-03-20 15:00 UTC | Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Alicia Park (Redwood AE), Samir Gupta (Redwood SE), Laura Chen (Hanwell - Procurement), Devon Reyes (Hanwell - Security), Marcus Holt (Hanwell - Engineering), Priya Anand (Hanwell - Legal)

Summary:
Quick procurement readout to align on MSA/DPA redlines, SLA thresholds, pilot pricing and the gating checklist for vendor acceptance. Hanwell has a strong emphasis on KMS/HSM and data residency. AE/SE clarified hosted vs dedicated options and next steps include sharing redline summary and running a perf bench.

Topics covered:
- MSA / DPA redline priorities (data retention, audit logs, sub-processing)
- SLA targets and remediation (p99 latency, uptime, maintenance windows)
- Pilot commercial path and 90-day pilot pricing model
- Security gating: KMS, SSO/SAML, SOC2 evidence, data residency
- Technical preflight: sample workload, perf bench, network egress costs
- Decision timeline and procurement committee requirements

Transcript:
[00:00] Alicia: Hey everyone, thanks for carving time — this is Alicia from Redwood, i'll kick things off. We wanted to run through the gating items you sent and make sure the procurement path is clear.
[00:12] Laura: Great thanks, Alicia. We're on a bit of a compressed timeline here, procurement would like a clear list of must-haves vs negotiables.
[00:20] Samir: Totally. We'll try to be explicit. Quick note, some of the product names in earlier docs got munged — "Red wood Dedicated" in one place, apologies, it's Redwood Dedicated.
[00:31] Devon: Haha, no worries. First order for us is KMS/HSM, we need to know if keys can be customer-managed and if there's an HSM-backed option, or at least BYOK with Cloud KMS.
[00:43] Alicia: Yes, we have both a hosted KMS integration and Private with customer-managed keys. For the hosted API we support external KMS via BYOK and for Redwood Private you can attach an HSM. There are some ops caveats — we'll put that in the redline summary.
[00:57] Marcus: A quick perf question — our workload is lots of short queries, 30–50 tokens most of the time with bursty peaks. What will be the p99 latency for hosted vs dedicated?
[01:10] Samir: With Dedicated we target sub-200ms p95 for short queries depending on model choice; p99 can vary — in practice around 350–700ms on the LLMs we tested. Hosted depends on tier, and we offer routing to lower-latency regions. We'll run a bench with your sample to be specific.
[01:28] Priya: On the DPA redlines, we flagged audit log granularity and subprocessor list. Can you provide a short mapping of what we can expect and what is non-negotiable?
[01:38] Alicia: Absolutely — we'll send a one-pager: Audit log fields, retention by default and options, plus subprocessor commitments. For anything that looks like a hard no we'll call it out.
[01:47] Laura: Egress fees — procurement needs clarity on potential variable costs, we have internal thresholds that mustn't be exceeded.
[01:54] Samir: We'll provide a breakdown: token-accounting model, typical per-token cost bands, and examples for your expected traffic patterns. Also we can show how caching/prefix-kv caching reduces egress costs in practice — though i keep saying "KV cash" by habit, haha.
[02:06] Devon: And SSO? We need SAML federation, with SCIM provisioning if possible.
[02:11] Alicia: SSO via SAML/SSO is supported; SCIM provisioning is available on enterprise tiers. We'll include the SAML metadata and SCIM endpoints in the pack.
[02:21] Marcus: For the pilot, what's the minimum commitment and pricing? Procurement prefers a time-bounded pilot vs a spend commit.
[02:28] Alicia: We typically offer a 90-day pilot with a capped usage credit and reduced rate for the Dedicated trial. Options: fully hosted trial (no infra commit), or dedicated pilot with reserved nodes for predictable latency. We'll lay out three options with pricing bands.
[02:43] Laura: If we do a dedicated pilot, how does rollback / fallback work? If you have outages do we get automatic fallback to a lower-tier model?
[02:51] Samir: Yes, we can set routing policies so requests fall back to a compatible model variant or region; automatic fallback is standard in the platform for resilience. We'll add the failover window and expected RTO to the SLA section.
[03:05] Priya: Any GDPR/data residency concerns? Some customers must keep PII in eu-west only.
[03:11] Alicia: We support regional deployment and private control planes that keep data in customer-chosen regions. We'll state the residency guarantees and third-party transfers in the DPA summary.
[03:20] Devon: On SOC 2 and certs — do you have a recent SOC 2 report and penetration test summary?
[03:26] Alicia: SOC 2 Type II report is available under NDA; we also have a pen-test summary. We'll share a link to the compliance pack after the call.
[03:34] Laura: Good — procurement will need the SOC2 to move forward.
[03:37] Marcus: For the perf bench: we'll give you a 24-hour trace and a synthetic sample. How long to run the bench and turn around results?
[03:44] Samir: We'll do a 2-hour dedicated run plus an extra spot check for burst behaviour and return a log bundle with p50/p95/p99 and token throughput within 4 business days.
[03:55] Laura: Okay that timeline works.
[03:57] Alicia: Regarding MSA clauses — there were three asks in your redlines: stricter indemnity, data retention shorter windows, and a specific SLAs carve-out. For pilot we'll usually accept a transit redline but enterprise indemnity changes need legal review.
[04:13] Priya: We may accept indemnity language tied to negligence but want the subprocessor notice window shortened.
[04:19] Alicia: Understood. We'll put the proposed language and note what needs legal escalation.
[04:23] Devon: Another note, we need full audit logs for all tokenized requests for at least 90 days, and a flag that indicates whether a request used the cache.
[04:33] Samir: We can log request id, model id, tokens in/out, and a cache-hit flag; retention configurable. We'll note the default retention vs extend options.
[04:44] Laura: On pricing — procurement asks for a not-to-exceed figure for month 1 and month 3 given our expected load. Can Redwood propose a predictable band?
[04:53] Alicia: We'll propose two billing models: usage-first with budget caps, or committed reserved nodes which smooth unit costs. We'll give you sample month 1/week 4 cost projections given your traffic.
[05:05] Marcus: About observability — what tooling does Redwood provide for tracing and token-level cost?
[05:11] Samir: Console includes token-level breakdowns, per-route dashboards, traces and request-level logs. We can open read-only access for your infra team during pilot.
[05:20] Laura: Procurement will insist on a security contact and an escalation ladder in the SLA.
[05:25] Alicia: We'll include a support SLA with named contacts and escalation tiers. Also note on maintenance windows — we aim for off-peak, and we'll include notification window in the SLA.
[05:37] Devon: Encryption at rest — is everything encrypted with customer-managed keys once provisioned?
[05:42] Samir: For Private yes; hosted supports CMEK/BYOK so you can manage keys. We'll detail the KMS flow.
[05:50] Priya: There's a legal question on subpoena / gov requests. Where do you stand on notifying customers?
[05:56] Alicia: We follow standard notification clauses; we push for notice where allowed by law and include law-enforcement request handling in the DPA. We'll surface limits for different jurisdictions.
[06:07] Laura: Ok, can you summarize deliverables and timing?
[06:12] Alicia: Sure — we'll send: (1) MSA/DPA redline summary + suggested language, (2) pilot pricing options and sample cost bands, (3) compliance pack (SOC2 / pen test) under NDA, (4) perf bench results after we run your sample payload. All by 2025-03-24 for the docs, perf by 2025-03-28.
[06:30] Marcus: Good. One small point — network egress: do you charge per region? How granular are those fees?
[06:37] Samir: Egress fees are regional and vary by route; we'll provide a per-region egress spreadsheet with examples for your expected traffic.
[06:45] Devon: Onboarding — procurement asks for a checklist for vendor gating. Can Redwood provide a one-page gating checklist for our internalops?
[06:52] Alicia: Yes we'll include a gating checklist: legal signoff, SOC2 review, SSO config, KMS confirmation, perf acceptance, budget sign.
[07:01] Laura: Excellent. If we hit all must-haves, procurement could greenlight a pilot the following week.
[07:07] Alicia: Great — we'll target the doc drop Friday and coordinate the perf window.
[07:12] Priya: Quick question — competitors were mentioned in our RFP, you have any reference customers in finance we can talk to?
[07:20] Alicia: We can share 2 anonymized references and a short case study; we'll need approvals but can include a fintech ref.
[07:28] Marcus: Please include any migration notes if we later want to move to a private deployment.
[07:33] Samir: We'll include migration path notes: model pinning, KV cache migration, and network peering options.
[07:40] Laura: Okay that's helpful. Any risks we should surface?
[07:44] Alicia: Primary risk: custom indemnity or unusual data-retention asks that require legal escalation and therefore extend timeline. Secondary: if your sample workload yields very high concurrent requests we might need dedicated nodes to hit tight p99 SLA — but that's what the bench will show.
[07:58] Devon: Sound good. One more item — billing terms: procurement needs Net 60 in some cases, is that negotiable?
[08:05] Alicia: Standard is Net 30; for enterprise we can discuss Net 45–60 on a case-by-case during commercial review. We'll note it.
[08:12] Laura: Thanks.
[08:14] Alicia: Alright — recap of next steps: we send docs, you send security questions answers, we run bench, then decision committee. Anything else?
[08:24] Priya: I'll coordinate legal redline priorities internally and flag anything that must go to counsel.
[08:29] Marcus: We'll prepare the perf payload and drop it in the shared folder.
[08:33] Devon: I'll fill the KMS bit.
[08:35] Alicia: Perfect. Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email and post the review packet in the shared drive.
[08:42] Laura: Thanks all.

End of meeting.

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-phrasing of product names (e.g., "Red wood Dedicated"), speaker overlap near timestamps 02:00–03:00, some filler (um, ah) removed for readability.

Attachments referenced: pricing-deck-v3.pdf (link: internal), redline-dpa-draft.docx (link: internal), perf-sample.zip (customer-supplied link).
